publications.summary: Responsibility October 27, 2026 The LEGO Group teams up with Sesame Street to inspire young children to fall in love with nature The LEGO Group and Sesame Workshop, the global nonprofit behind Sesame Street, have launched three new videos, funded by the LEGO Foundation, encouraging children aged 4 to 6 to discover the natural world through play. Featuring Elmo, Cookie Monster and other Sesame Street friends, the videos introduce children to bats, butterflies and worms before inviting them to build habitats using LEGO bricks and everyday craft materials. The LEGO Group’s free activity guides and printables help families and educators extend the experience through hands-on play at home and in community settings.

publications.title: BrickLink issues statement on downtime
publications.summary: BrickLink has now been offline for almost a week and a few minutes before it was estimated to be back online, at 18:00 CET today, the website has been updated with a brief comment regarding its status, which follows: 'We took BrickLink offline after identifying unusual activity on the platform. Our immediate priority was to secure the site, protect our members and ensure the integrity of BrickLink. Before bringing the site back online, we need to fully understand what has happened. That means containing the issue, investigating how it happened and checking for related issues. This work is still on-going and we appreciate your patience while we work to get things back online as soon as possible.' The statement is pretty vague and I cannot speculate on possible reasons for this issue, but the comment that they are still trying to understand what happened does not exactly fill me with confidence. publications.title: BrickLink downtime continues
publications.summary: As you may have noticed, BrickLink has been down since late last week, and it's just been announced that it will remain offline until at least Wednesday evening. That impacts us here because we hot link to minifigure images on the BrickLink server, which is why our listings are not currently showing them, and we also uses its API to gather prices and availability of sets, parts, and minifigs. No announcement, or indeed any communication at all, has been made about why it's been offline for so long, so we will have to draw our own conclusions. I guess it's possible that the recent well publicised PHP issues have something to do with it. In the meantime, the independent LEGO marketplace BrickOwl remains online and ready to sate your ABS cravings. Are you a buyer or a seller affected by the outage? What do you make of it? © 2026 Brickset.com . Republication prohibited without prior permission.

publications.title: Competition: Build a Restaurant of the World
publications.summary: It's been five years since we last held a building competition, so it's high time we arranged another one! The four Restaurants of the World that were offered as gifts with purchase during the year were great fun and well received. We want you to build one in the same style. Simple as that. Your model should: Be built on a 10x12 stud base Have a single-storey building that's 8x10 in size Be open at the back Have an oversized representation of the food that's being sold on the roof Optionally include a minifig Not use AI to enhance its appearance You could make a seaside fish and chip shop, an ice cream parlour, coffee booth, or perhaps something that's common in your country: it's entirely up to you! We encourage you to build with real bricks, but digital entries will be accepted, as long as they could be built in real life. Feel free to add 'stickers' for the sign/menu etc. Entries will be judged on their originality, how well they capture the essence of the location and/or the food they are selling, use of the space and, of course, the design of the rooftop appendage. Three prizes will be awarded, with the grand prize being 11387 Holiday House. Second and third prizes will be announced later. To enter, add a couple of photos of your entry to the group on Flickr , upload to Instagram with the hashtag #bricksetrowcompetition, or email your entry to competition@brickset.com by Monday, 30th November. Good luck! © 2026 Brickset.com . Republication prohibited without prior permission.

publications.title: Review: 72161 Drone Search for Mythical Mew
publications.summary: Long before Grogu, another cute, rare, powerful, and seemingly ageless creature was sought after for its special properties—in the hopes of engineering ultimate beings . With this set, you too can search for such a mythical marvel, but hopefully for some less nefarious purposes. Back in my day, Mew was a schoolyard legend, as finding it needed a glitchy miracle, and the process was not a simple internet search away! Now kids can just use a drone—and a surprisingly fun one at that! Please note, this set does not contain a SMART Brick. Continue reading » © 2026 Brickset.com . Republication prohibited without prior permission.
